content.name: Harriet Penrose
content.title: Lead UX Designer
content.summary: Lead UX designer with 13 years in agency, insurance, rail and energy, now heading a team of five designers for a renewable energy supplier. Combines a psychology background with service design, and the redesigned switching journey I led raised online sign-ups by 31% while halving drop-out at the meter step.

experience.title: Junior UX Designer
bullets: Produced wireframes, site maps and clickable prototypes for charity and higher education websites.
Ran guerrilla usability tests in cafés and libraries, five to eight people per round, and wrote up findings for clients.
Helped a university client restructure its course pages, cutting calls to the admissions office about entry requirements.

experience.title: UX Designer
bullets: Designed the online claims journey for home and car policies, handling about 4,000 claims a month.
Replaced a 14-page claim form with a step-by-step flow, raising online claim completion from 49% to 70%.
Introduced plain-English content testing with the content design team, reducing complaints about unclear wording.
Built the company's first accessibility checklist, aligned to WCAG 2.1 AA, and trained 30 staff in how to use it.

experience.title: Senior UX Designer
bullets: Led UX for a journey-planning and ticketing app used by about 1.5 million passengers a year.
Designed disruption messaging with operations staff, so passengers saw alternatives within seconds of a cancellation.
Ran diary studies with commuters and occasional travellers, which reshaped the season ticket renewal flow.
Mentored three mid-level designers, two of whom moved into senior roles.

experience.title: Lead UX Designer
bullets: Head a team of five product and service designers covering sign-up, billing, smart meter and help journeys.
Led the redesign of the switching journey, increasing online sign-ups by 31% and halving drop-out at the meter details step.
Set up a research operations practice with a participant panel of 900 customers, including people in vulnerable circumstances.
Work with the Head of Product on a £1.2 million annual roadmap, deciding priorities with evidence from research and analytics.
Run a shared design system with engineering, cutting UI inconsistencies flagged in QA by more than half.

education.details: Dissertation on decision-making under time pressure

courses.name: Certified Professional for Usability and User Experience (CPUX-F)
